answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The nebula multiplier is published, charged in garden, and yarrow lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1844 identities would post 1970 proofs and burn roughly 61 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
